Des Würzburger Bischofs Reinhard Bestätigungsbrief eines Gütertausches. 1178.

In nomine sanete et individue trinitatis. Reinhardus dei gratia Würtzburg. eccl. Episcopus. Notum esse cupimus omnibus tam presentibus quam post futuris, predium quod- dam fratrum de Brunnebach in parochia Reicholsheim silum esse, sc. curiam, que dicitur Lengenvelt cum suis adjacen- tii.s et curiam, que dicitur Brunnebach cum suis adjacentiis, de quibus tertia pars deeime attinebat eidem parochie. Ipsi vero fratres usi tam suo, quam aliorum bonorum virorum con- silio, domino Bopponi Coiniti de Wertheim, qui jure beueficii 15 derimam illam ab episcopatu habuit, de rebus suis in tantum contulerunt, quud ipse cum nubis resignavit, et duo predia nimm in Waldenhuaen, alterum in Sahsenhusen, ad concam- bium illius decime super altare ejusdem ecclesie, sc. Reichola- heim manu sua et uxoris sue legitime delegavit. His ita perac- tis presente Offene et advocato ejusdem parochie, postquam etiam vidimus homines seped. parochie, quibus res ea nota erat, juramento confirmasse, quod predia, que in concam- bium decime illius data erunt, multo majoris pretii quam ipsa decima essent. Ut firmior fides huic rei adhiberetur, qui- busdam fidelibus nostris, ut huic concambio interessent, fide- liter commisimus Adelberto de Hohenloch. Thimone de Win desheim. Arnoldo. Conrado duobus filiis Ruperti de Ussen- keim. Ministerialibus: Herbordo de Ussenkeim. Gumperto et Adalberto de Wertheim et adhuc quam pluribus aliis, qui concordantes juramento predict. hominum, rogatu predicti Comitis et pro remedio anime nostre deeimam illam b. Marie in Brunnebach delegavimus. Quod ergo factum est, presentis scripti pagina confirmavimus eique auetoritatem im- pressione sigilli nostri dedimus. Itidemque Mengenlano tres et dimidiam marcam, quo et ille nihilominus domino sno Bopponi Comiti de Wertheim decimas praescriptas resignaret. Qui tandem in nostras manus illas resignavit, quatenus solemni donatione super reliquias sanctorum in Brunnebach, Deo et loci pre- fati fratribus in honorem b. Marie Dei genitricis offerremus ac perpetualiter possidendas confirmaremus. Nos igitur retri butions divine intuitu per manus proprias super reliquias prescriptas sepefatas decimas delegavimus et presentis privilegio scripti atque nostri sigilli impressione factum sub anathemate et officii nostri auctoritate confirmavimus. In nomine sanete et indiuidue trinitatis. Boppo dei gratia Comes de Wertheym. Pax, uictoria regnumque per nenne Christi et ecclesie feliciter in euum permaneat. Quoniam ea que in mundo sunt agili fluxu et celeri cursu cuneta pretereunt et ea que non sunt superueniunt, mirandum non est, si mortalium queque facta quasi cum ipsis morientia recedunt et quasi non fuerint sie uniuersa erunt. Proinde uero est quod rationi bene congruit, scilicet quod sacra priuilegiorum sanetione quelibet pia nobilium ac poten- tum gesta in posterum muniantur. Ut igitur hec presens do natio uniuersis fidelibus Christo et ecclesie deuotis semper pateat, hec mea testimentalis tuba in omni personet euo. Quoniam ego Boppo dei gratia Comes de Wertheym nobilitate prepollens diuiciis deliciisque alfluens grauibus delictis et noxialibus peccatis dominum deum grauiter offendisse intra me extimui, meque ad placandum ipsum regem celorum ultra maris alueum Ihrosolimam iturum deuotaui, ibique sanctissimum sepulchrum domini christianissima fide uisitaturum optaui, summopere sperans meque consolans per regem et sacerdo- tem uerum Samaritanum nostrum miseros errores meos abo- \\ertbeim. entries.english:
Confirmation by Reinhard, Bishop of Würzburg, of an exchange of property. 1178.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity. Reinhard, by the grace of God Bishop of the Church of Würzburg, wishes it to be known to all, present and future, that certain property of the brothers of Brombach in the parish of Reicholzheim consists of the manor called Lengenfeld with its appurtenances and the manor called Brombach with its appurtenances, from which a third part of the tithe belonged to that parish. The brothers, acting on their own counsel and that of other good men, granted so much of their property to Lord Boppo, Count von Wertheim, who held that tithe from the bishopric as a benefice, that he surrendered it to us; in exchange for that tithe, with his own hand and that of his lawful wife, he assigned two estates to the altar of the same church, namely Reicholzheim: one at Waldenhausen and the other at Sachsenhausen.

This having been done in the presence of Offene, advocate of that parish, and after we had also seen the people of the aforesaid parish, who knew the matter, confirm on oath that the estates given in exchange for the tithe were worth much more than the tithe itself, we faithfully commissioned certain of our faithful men to witness the exchange: Adelbert von Hohenlohe, Thimo von Windsheim, Arnold, Conrad and the two sons of Ruprecht von Uissigheim; among our ministerials, Herbord von Uissigheim, Gumbert and Adelbert von Wertheim, and many others. In agreement with the sworn testimony of the aforesaid people, at the request of the aforesaid Count and for the salvation of our soul, we assigned that tithe to Saint Mary at Brombach. We have confirmed what was done by this written charter and given it authority through the impression of our seal. If anyone in the future should presumptuously or maliciously attempt to break or weaken this grant, let him be anathema.

Clerical witnesses: Godefridus, provost; Persius, dean; Godefridus, scholasticus; Albertus, custodian; Godefridus, cantor; Bertholdus, provost; Eberhard von Marmore; Godefridus von Crutheim; Conrad Cellarius; Dietrich von Bebenburg; Berengerus. Lay witnesses: Boppo, Count von Wertheim; Sigebodo von Zimmern; Crafto von Boxberg; Wolframus von Bebenburg; Otto von Eschenhausen; Crafto von Rettersheim; Heinrich, schultheiss; Hartmund von Bischofswinden; Wolframus von Brosoldesheim and his brother Conrad; Bilingus; Cadelohas and his brother; Wuhardus; Adelhun; Arnoldus; Hermannus; Wolfolt; and many others. Done in the year of the Lord 1178, during the reign of the glorious Roman Emperor Frederick, when Boppo was urban count.

XIIa. Confirmation by Bishop Reinhard of Würzburg for Brombach Monastery concerning tithes at Lengenfeld and Oberbrunn (Schafhof). 1180.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity and its inseparable unity. I, Reinhard, by the grace of God Bishop of the Holy See of Würzburg, have been called by divine mercy to the lofty height of the pontificate so that, as God’s servant, we may provide support and assistance to God’s poor and bestow benefits upon them. Such acts befit our dignity, adorn our office, and enhance our reputation. Therefore we wish it known to all, present and future, how we granted this favor to the religious servants of God at the place in our diocese called Brombach: the persons who held two thirds of the tithes of the monastery itself and of its two nearby granges, Oberbrunn and Lengenfeld, as benefices were to redeem them and hold them forever for their own use.

The brothers gave 45 talents to the knight Crafto von Rudingsheim so that he would surrender the tithes to his lord Gernod von Roelbach. They then gave Gernod ten [talents] and a palfrey worth one talent so that he, in turn, would surrender those tithes to his lord, Mengenlan von Aschaffenburg. Likewise, they gave Mengenlan three and a half marks so that he, in turn, would surrender the aforesaid tithes to his lord, Boppo, Count von Wertheim. Boppo then surrendered them into our hands so that we might solemnly bestow them upon God and the brothers of the aforesaid place, in honor of Saint Mary, Mother of God, on the relics of the saints at Brombach, and confirm them to be held forever. Therefore, in view of divine reward, we ourselves transferred the aforesaid tithes upon the relics and confirmed this act under anathema and by the authority of our office, through this charter of privilege and the impression of our seal.

To ensure that this pious act remains more firmly in force among our successors, we received in exchange from the religious men a certain manor which they had bought from Lutold von Gundelsheim, on the condition that every year, on the Feast of the Annunciation of the Blessed Mary, they offer at the high altar of the Church of Saint Kilian two candles weighing one pound each, as a gift, and thereby make the exchange known to all. If any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing the terms of this charter, should in future rashly oppose it or presume in any way to disturb, molest, or trouble those brothers in the collection of the aforesaid tithes, let that person be deprived of the fellowship of all Christians, barred from receiving the sacred body and blood of the Lord, and condemned in the world to come to the eternal torments of hell with the devil and his companions.

Witnesses: clergy—Persius, dean of the cathedral; Godefridus, cantor; Albertus, custodian; Godefridus, scholasticus; Eberhard von Marmore; Godefridus, porter; Beringerus von Cimbre; Wuherus, provost of Saint John the Baptist; Albertus, dean of the same church; Tieno, deacon; Herold, abbot of Saint Burkhard; Babinold, abbot of Zell. Laymen: the Emperor’s sons Otto and Conrad; Count Boppo von Wertheim; Sigebodo von Zimmern and his son Heinrich; Berenger von Phasich; Tragebodo von Engilstat; Berenger von Gamenburg; Otto von Eschenhausen. Ministerials: Engelhard von Biebelrieth; Ruger and Otto von Homburg; Hermann, chamberlain; Gerhard von Bastheim; Heinrich von Gollach; Boto and Heinrich, schultheiss, of Würzburg; Eggehardus Granius; Heroldus; Arnoldus; Wuhardus; Adelhur von Würzburg; and many others. Done in the year of the Lord 1180, during the reign of Emperor Frederick, when Boppo was prefect of the city, in the thirteenth indiction.

XIIb. Count Boppo von Wertheim grants toll exemption throughout his county to the Cistercian Abbey of Altenberg on the Lower Rhine before his journey to the Holy Sepulchre. 1183.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity. Boppo, by the grace of God Count von Wertheim. May peace, victory, and the kingdom of Christ and the Church endure happily forever. Since everything in this world passes swiftly away, and what was not there before comes in its place, it is no wonder that the deeds of mortals pass away as if they died with them, and all things become as though they had never been. It is therefore right and reasonable that the sacred authority of privileges should secure for the future every pious deed of noble and powerful people. So that this present donation may always be known to all the faithful devoted to Christ and the Church, let this testament of mine resound for all time.

I, Boppo, by the grace of God Count von Wertheim, distinguished in nobility and abundantly supplied with wealth and comforts, considered that I had gravely offended the Lord God through serious transgressions and harmful sins. To appease Him, I vowed to travel overseas to Jerusalem, the King of Heaven, and wished to visit the Lord’s most holy sepulchre in the Christian faith, hoping and consoling myself greatly that through our true King and Priest, the Good Samaritan, my wretched errors would be erased and the wounds and sicknesses of my soul healed there completely.

As I reflected upon these salutary vows, I went to the beloved place of Bergen on the Rhine. There, for the sake of earning eternal life for myself and my dear ones, living and dead, I donated to the Lord Jesus Christ, His immaculate mother, the perpetual Virgin Mary, and all the brothers there devoted to God, in perpetual and stable service, all tolls on their goods transported by ship which, by royal right, I could exact within my jurisdiction and collect for my own use. I made and confirmed this grant irrevocably before suitable witnesses, together with my beloved wife Cunigunda and my only children.

As reliable proof of this donation, I firmly established that all members of this monastery, on horseback or on foot, crossing my castle without a ship, shall always travel safely and securely, without injury or burden from me or my successors, throughout all the territories under my authority and rule, and return home safely; in return they shall offer us their devout prayers in the Lord. To ensure that this donation remains intact and unimpaired in its proper force, the impression of our seal confirms it forever, perpetually and irrevocably.

Witnesses: the entire sacred convent of that monastery; Abbot Eberolf of Brombach; Conrad von Wichardesheim; Arnold, son of Trutmann; Gumbert, toll collector of that same Count Boppo; Friedrich; and many others. Done in the year of the Lord 1183, in the first indiction, while the most blessed Lord Lucius, by the grace of God Pope, presided over the apostolic see; the invincible and most glorious Lord Frederick, by the grace of God Roman Emperor, ruled in the twentieth year of his empire; Lord Philip, by the grace of God Archbishop of the Holy Church of Cologne, and Lord Gozwin, most reverend abbot, held office; and Lord Reinhard, reverend Bishop of the Church of Würzburg.

[Printed in Th. J. Lacomblet, *Urkundenbuch für die Geschichte des Niederrheins*, Düsseldorf, 1840, vol. 1, p. 345, no. 489.]
